html:
The United Nations mission set up in 1991 to watch the ceasefire in Western Sahara and to hold a referendum in which the Sahrawis would choose between independence and joining Morocco.

The ceasefire began on 6 September 1991 and largely held for 29 years. The vote never happened: Morocco and the Polisario Front could not agree on who could vote, and Morocco later offered only autonomy. In November 2020 the Polisario declared the ceasefire over after a clash at Guerguerat, and in December the United States recognised Moroccan sovereignty. The mission still has observers in the territory, and Laayoune is its headquarters. See also the Western Sahara War.
sum: The United Nations mission set up in 1991 to watch the ceasefire in Western Sahara and to hold a referendum in which the Sahrawis would choose between independence and joining Morocco.
